processing: A strong black tea brew mixed with evaporated milk instead of the condensed milk of teh tarik. Sugar is usually added unless you ask otherwise.
harvest_season: Not applicable; it is made with whatever strong black tea the stall uses.
appearance_dry: Often fine tea dust or small broken leaf, as with other kopitiam tea.
appearance_liquor: An opaque caramel brown from the evaporated milk.
appearance_wet: Fine dark tea dust, strained out before serving.
taste_profile: Strong, slightly bitter tea softened by the rounded milkiness of evaporated milk, with sweetness to order.

brewing.notes: Brew very strong, strain, then add evaporated milk and sugar to taste. Kurang manis means less sweet; kosong means no sugar.

vintage_note: It has no vintages or seasons. It is a made-to-order drink at kopitiams and stalls, with a glass made from cheap strong tea, so judge it by the stall and not by the leaf.
description:
Teh-C is the kopitiam milk tea made with evaporated milk, a close relative of teh tarik without the condensed milk. The C stands for Carnation, a popular brand of evaporated milk.

A very strong brew of black tea, often from dust, is strained and mixed with the milk. Evaporated milk gives body with little sweetness of its own, so the sugar is a separate decision.

The order matters. Sugar goes in unless you say otherwise: ask for kurang manis for less, kosong for none, and ais for ice.

In Sarawak look for Teh-C Peng Special, a three-layered iced version of tea, milk and palm sugar syrup. To try one at home, use a strong, cheap black tea rather than a fine one.
history:
Teh-C grew out of the same milk tea culture as teh tarik, in which Indian Muslim vendors on the Malay Peninsula played a central part. Its own origin date is not recorded.

The name itself ties the drink to canned evaporated milk, through the Carnation brand.
